learnings.question: When analyzing word frequency across the text of the Quran, approximately what cumulative percentage of the total text do the top 20 most frequent words actually make up?
learnings.learning: Contrary to the common expectation under the Pareto Principle (80/20 rule) that the top 20 most frequent words might account for 80% of the Quran, data analysis reveals they only accumulate to approximately 20.83% of the text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: Which Scrum artifact is used to visualize the progress of a Sprint and track remaining work?
learnings.learning: In Scrum, a Burndown Chart is the artifact used to visualize the progress of a Sprint and monitor remaining work to help determine if the team is on schedule.

learnings.question: According to 1880s research by Hermann Ebbinghaus, approximately what percentage of new information is forgotten within 24 hours without active recall?
learnings.learning: In the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus demonstrated that humans forget roughly 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In Quran 51:56, what is identified as the foundational purpose for the creation of jinn and mankind?
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 clarifies the foundational purpose of existence with the divine declaration: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.'

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state offers the highest power savings and has the longest wake-up time by placing the device in an almost completely powered-down state?
learnings.learning: PCIe power management balances responsiveness and energy efficiency across a spectrum of states, ranging from fully active (L0) to almost completely powered down (L2), with deeper states providing greater power savings at the expense of longer wake-up delays.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe
